title: U.S. House · Michigan's 1st District
area: Michigan's 1st Congressional District — the Upper Peninsula and the northern Lower Peninsula (Traverse City, Marquette, Sault Ste. Marie).

context.text: Cook Political Report rated Michigan's 1st District R+11 for the 2026 cycle. Donald Trump won the district 59.9%–38.7% in 2024.

Incumbent Jack Bergman defeated Matthew DenOtter and Justin Michal in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 74.7% of the vote. Callie Barr defeated Kyle Blomquist and Wayne Stiles in the Democratic primary with 56.3% of the vote.

candidates.name: Jack Bergman
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 74.7% of the vote

summary.text: Bergman is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 1st District, first elected in 2016. He retired from the U.S. Marine Corps as a lieutenant general after 40 years of service before entering politics.

background.text: Born in Shakopee, Minnesota, in 1947; earned a bachelor's degree in business from Gustavus Adolphus College (1969) and an MBA from the University of Western Florida.
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1969 to 2009, retiring as a lieutenant general; upon election to Congress became the highest-ranking combat veteran ever elected to Congress.
Worked as a commercial pilot and owned a medical technology business before being elected to Congress.

priorities.text: Says he has used his role on the House Veterans' Affairs Committee to work on toxic exposure, mental health, and expanding Veterans' access to community care.

Highlights his work supporting Michigan's agriculture industry, including advocacy for the USMCA trade agreement and against unfair foreign trade practices affecting Michigan cherry, apple, dairy, and other growers.
Points to his role securing Great Lakes Restoration Initiative funding and combating invasive species such as Asian carp as a priority for protecting the region's natural resources.

positions.summary: A member of the Congressional Pro-Life Caucus, has supported the Pain-Capable Unborn Child Protection Act, which would ban abortions after 20 weeks of pregnancy, along with other legislation restricting abortion.
positions.quote: Congressman Bergman has also supported the Pain Capable Unborn Child Protection Act (H.R.1080) which bans abortions after the 20th week of pregnancy.

positions.summary: Has cosponsored or sponsored legislation to expand border wall construction, penalize sanctuary jurisdictions, and tighten the asylum process, and supported additional border wall and security funding in 2019.
positions.quote: Congressman Bergman has supported important policies to secure our border and put our Country first. He cosponsored legislation to address the current crisis and some of its root causes, such as H.R.88 - the BUILD WALL Act of 2021.

positions.summary: States on his campaign site that he stands for protecting Second Amendment rights.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs; Health) and the House Committee on Armed Services, chairing the Readiness Subcommittee, and on the House Committee on the Budget.

candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 56.3% of the vote

summary.text: Barr is an attorney and former high school English teacher from Traverse City running as the Democratic nominee against incumbent Jack Bergman.
